summary: Sequatchie County, TN lookout site at 2,244 ft, marked removed on the Tennessee tower list. No build, staffing or removal date found; no site description.

facts.status_note: Marked removed on the Tennessee tower list, which gives no removal date.

evidence.supports: the list author gave unofficial names to towers not named on USGS maps or the state list
evidence.quote: I have given unofficial names to towers that were not named on the USGS maps or on the list of towers provided by the state forestry office

evidence.supports: CCC reported to have built 98 lookout houses and towers in Tennessee in the 1930s
evidence.quote: it is reported that the CCC was responsible for the construction of 98 lookout houses and towers in Tennessee during this period

evidence.supports: first state forestry fire tower: wood Cagle tower of about 1933 atop Wolfpen Mountain, Sequatchie County
evidence.quote: the TDF states that its first fire tower was the ca. 1933 wood-frame Cagle Fire Lookout Tower (not extant) atop Wolfpen Mountain in Sequatchie County

evidence.supports: the Cagle tower was demolished and replaced with a steel-frame tower named for Wolfpen Mountain, at an unknown date
evidence.quote: The Cagle Fire Lookout Tower was later demolished and replaced with the Wolfpen Mountain Fire Lookout Tower (an Aeromotor steel-frame Model LS-40)

evidence.supports: most former tower locations are now private property
evidence.quote: Many have been removed, and most locations are now private property

evidence.supports: the page advises against climbing the towers
evidence.quote: You are advised not to climb the towers

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (Multiple Property Documentation Form)

notes_for_editor: Only the Tennessee list places this tower; no other source found names Price Mountain as a lookout. No build, staffing, fire or removal date. Elevation 684 m and coordinates (35.4517, -85.5001) match the record and the tnlandforms waypoint SQT003. The name may be the list author's own (his note on unofficial names); worth checking the USGS name and any Tennessee Division of Forestry records if a human has access. The MPS context on the Cagle tower and the 98 CCC towers is regional background only; no source ties Price Mountain to either.
